approach: Fix both root causes. (a) athena.toml: check_timeout_s 900 -> 1800; the schema is already u64, so config.rs is untouched. (b) checks.rs gets one shared definition of "killed at its deadline": a note-prefix constant used by run_check when it writes the deadline note, plus a pub fn `timed_out(&CheckRun)` (passed false, exit_code None, note starts with that prefix; the kill-switch note and a spawn failure do not match). disk.rs gets a CHECK_TIMEOUT reason prefix ("environment: check timed out"), is_environment_reason accepts it, and `check_timeout_reason(name, secs, limit_s, job)` builds the closing text ("<name> killed at 905s of 1800s limit; this is the environment, not the work ..., `athena retry <job>`"). In `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs), right after the `checks ...` line is printed and before mark_pre_existing, if any fresh check run is `timed_out`, close via `self.failure(ctx, reason)` with verification_passed None, remove the verify dir and return, like the existing low-disk-before-verifier early return. Because the closing is Failed with an environment reason, settle_resume_marks keeps the Checks-stage resume mark and resumable_stop / `athena retry` treat the job as held, not rejected. A real nonzero exit stays a failed check and goes on to verification and rejection as today. Tests use a cfg(test) thread-local check seam in run/mod.rs (same pattern as replay_seam) that SnapExec::exec consults first, so the fake runner supplies only the CheckRun while all classification code is production code. Part (3), the athena status durations report, and status.rs are out of scope and not touched.

decisions.choice: Detect a timeout with a shared helper in checks.rs over the existing deadline note (`timed_out(&CheckRun)`), with run_check building its note from the same constant.
decisions.reason: No new CheckRun field or record change is allowed. Sharing the constant keeps the classifier and the producer of the note in step; a real-runner test in checks.rs proves a genuinely killed check satisfies it. Requiring exit_code None and passed false keeps a passing check, a real failure and a kill-switch kill out.

rejected.option: Add a `timed_out: bool` field to CheckRun
rejected.why: Changes a record type and its serialisation; the brief forbids it.

rejected.option: Match the text 'killed at the deadline' inline in run/mod.rs
rejected.why: A second copy of the string can drift from the one in run_check and silently turn timeouts back into rejections.

rejected.option: Treat any exit_code None as a timeout
rejected.why: Spawn failures, the kill switch and skipped/reused checks also have no exit code.

decisions.choice: Reuse the environment-reason path with a new prefix `environment: check timed out`, accepted by disk::is_environment_reason.
decisions.reason: resumable_stop, settle_resume_marks (keeps the resume mark) and retry already key on is_environment_reason, so the job is held and retried with no new state.

rejected.why: TimedOut means the producer or verifier agent timed out and is handled by timeout_seed; resumable_stop does not resume it.

rejected.option: A separate resumable list for check timeouts
rejected.why: Duplicates the mechanism and requires touching scope_guard and reading.rs.

decisions.choice: Stop in check_and_verify before mark_pre_existing, the replay and the verifier, only on a fresh (not resumed) set of check runs.
decisions.reason: A timeout says nothing about the work, so no verifier cost should be spent and no pre-existing marking applies. Resumed recorded checks all passed, so they cannot hold a timeout. The Checks-stage resume mark is kept, so retry re-runs only the checks.

rejected.option: Let verification run and filter the 'check test failed' reason afterward
rejected.why: Spends a verifier run and still ends in a verdict-based rejection path.

decisions.choice: Fake runner = cfg(test) thread-local seam inside run/mod.rs consulted at the top of SnapExec::exec (after refuse_if_stopped).
decisions.reason: The brief lists no lib.rs, so the seam lives in a listed file, following the replay_seam precedent. The fake returns only a CheckRun; classification, closing, resume mark and retry eligibility are production code.

rejected.why: Needs config rewrites and slows the suite; the real kill is still covered at unit level in checks.rs.

rejected.option: A trait-object runner field on Athena
rejected.why: Touches lib.rs and every Athena constructor, more than this change needs.

decisions.choice: Print the limit actually applied (jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s) with the measured run.duration, whole seconds, in the closing reason (shown on the `failed` line); keep the existing `checks ... (Ns)` line.
decisions.reason: The failure reason is recorded and shown, so a stranger sees '905s of 1800s limit' without reading code.

rejected.option: Parse the limit from the note
rejected.why: Fragile; the config value is the source.

files.purpose: Governance file listed as deliverable: [budget] check_timeout_s 900 -> 1800.

Add DEADLINE_NOTE_PREFIX, deadline_note(Duration) and pub fn timed_out(&CheckRun); run_check builds its deadline note through deadline_note; unit tests (real killed check satisfies timed_out; failure, pass, kill-switch, spawn failure, skipped run do not).
Add CHECK_TIMEOUT reason prefix, check_timeout_reason(name, duration_s, limit_s, job), extend is_environment_reason, update docs, unit tests.

check_and_verify stops on a timed-out fresh check run as an environment stop; cfg(test) check_seam used by SnapExec::exec; tests for timeout vs real failure, message contents and repository config value.
Unreleased entry for the 1800 s limit and timeout-as-environment-stop, citing job 20261026-232434-6wfq.

steps: checks.rs: add `DEADLINE_NOTE_PREFIX = "killed at the deadline of "`, `deadline_note(timeout: Duration) -> String` and `pub fn timed_out(run: &CheckRun) -> bool`; replace the inline format! in run_check with deadline_note(ctx.timeout). Add/extend a unit test asserting timed_out on a real killed `sleep` check, and negative-case tests (exit 3, pass, kill-switch note, spawn failure, skipped_run).

disk.rs: add `pub const CHECK_TIMEOUT: &str = "environment: check timed out"`; add `pub fn check_timeout_reason(name: &str, duration_s: f64, limit_s: u64, job: &JobId) -> String` giving "environment: check timed out: {name} killed at {duration:.0}s of {limit}s limit; this is the environment, not the work. `athena retry {job}`, or raise [budget] check_timeout_s"; make is_environment_reason accept LOW_DISK or CHECK_TIMEOUT prefixes; update docs; add unit tests `a_check_timeout_reason_is_an_environment_reason` and a text test.

run/mod.rs: add module-level `#[cfg(test)] mod check_seam` (thread_local RefCell<Option<Rc<dyn Fn(&CheckSpec) -> CheckRun>>>, `install` returning a Drop guard, `run`), modelled on the replay_seam; in SnapExec::exec, after refuse_if_stopped, `#[cfg(test)] if let Some(run) = check_seam::run(spec) { return Ok(run); }`.

run/mod.rs check_and_verify: after the `checks     ...` ui line and only inside `if !resumed_checks`, find the first run with crate::checks::timed_out; if found, keep closing.happened.changed_paths, set closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &crate::disk::check_timeout_reason(&run.name, run.duration.value().unwrap_or(0.0), jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s, &id)), restore changed_paths, set verification_passed = None, remove verify_dir with crate::pin::remove_tree, return Ok(closing). Place it before mark_pre_existing, the produce-dir removal, the replay stage and the verifier gate. Leave the recorded_checks mark unset so the Checks resume mark stays.

run/mod.rs tests (in produce_and_verify_order_tests): (a) `a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_is_an_environment_stop` (905 s CheckRun built with checks::deadline_note; assert Failed, is_environment_reason, resumable_stop, not Rejected, no verifier call, resume mark at Checks, reason and captured `failed     ` UI line contain '905s of 1800s limit'); (b) `a_real_failing_check_is_still_a_rejection` (exit_code Some(1); assert Rejected, not environment); (c) `repository_check_timeout_is_1800` parsing include_str!(athena.toml). Optionally (d) retry after the timeout with the seam removed resumes without planner or producer, modelled on low_disk_before_the_verifier_resumes_without_planner_or_producer.

CHANGELOG.md: add under [Unreleased] an entry: cause (900 s limit under a 750-940 s suite; job 20261026-232434-6wfq rejected with 'check test failed' after 591 tests, exit code none, 905 s, while the verifier's own run passed), the 1800 s limit, the timed-out check now closing as `environment: check timed out` (held, resumable by `athena retry`) with measured duration against the limit, and that the athena status duration report is a separate follow-up.
Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: A non-timeout failure is misread as a timeout and a rejection becomes a hold.
risks.mitigation: timed_out requires passed == false, exit_code == None and the exact note prefix, which only run_check's deadline branch writes (via the shared constant). Unit tests cover the negative cases and the companion rejection test covers the end-to-end path.

risks.risk: The note text changes in run_check later and the classifier silently stops matching.
risks.mitigation: A real-runner unit test in checks.rs (short deadline, real `sleep`) asserts timed_out on the actual output of run_check, so the constant and classifier cannot drift apart.

risks.risk: The early return leaves state retry cannot resume from, or leaves the verify directory behind.
risks.mitigation: The early return mirrors the existing before-verifier one (failure, clear verification_passed, remove verify dir); the test asserts the resume mark remains and resumable_stop is true.

risks.risk: The test seam leaks into production or between parallel tests.
risks.mitigation: The seam is #[cfg(test)] only, per-thread, cleared by a Drop guard, and returns early only when installed.
The fake returns a fixed 905.0 s with no sleeping; the real-runner test uses a ~300 ms deadline like the existing baseline timeout test.

risks.risk: The printed limit differs from the one applied.
risks.mitigation: The limit printed is read from jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s, the same value passed to the runner.

demonstrations.method: Content check plus a config test. Grep athena.toml for `check_timeout_s = 1800`; Grep crates/athena-data/src/config.rs for `pub check_timeout_s: u64` (file unchanged; git diff shows no change). A new test in run/mod.rs (step 6c) parses the repository file with `athena_data::Config::parse(include_str!("../../../../athena.toml"))` and asserts budget.check_timeout_s == 1800. No seam needed; the repository file is the fixture.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-core repository_check_timeout_is_1800 && cargo test --locked -p athena-data
demonstrations.observes: The test passes with 1800 and the existing athena-data config tests still pass, so the schema accepts it unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: If athena.toml still said 900 the config test asserting 1800 fails; if the schema type changed, the athena-data tests would not compile or pass.

demonstrations.method: New test in produce_and_verify_order_tests, run through the production entry point `Athena::go` (-> produce_and_verify -> check_and_verify) with the existing athena_with/base_script/Docs fixtures (fake agent driver, temp git repo, plenty_of_space gate). Preconditions: planning off, disk gate passes. The fake check runner is a thread-local seam (new cfg(test) module `check_seam` in run/mod.rs, added in plan step 4; it does not exist today) installed with a Drop guard and consulted at the top of SnapExec::exec. It returns a CheckRun with passed false, exit_code None, duration 905.0 s, note = checks::deadline_note(900s) built by the production helper. The seam holds no classification logic. After go, read Finished and assert state == Failed, disk::is_environment_reason(&reason), resumable_stop(Closed(Failed), Some(&reason)), state != Rejected, no verifier invocation (counting()), and read_resume(job) is still Some at ResumeStage::Checks.
demonstrations.observes: The job closes Failed with an `environment: check timed out` reason, is resumable, kept its resume mark, and the verifier never ran.
demonstrations.fails_without: If check_and_verify did not classify a timed-out run, the job would reach verification and end Rejected ('check probe failed'); the assertions on Failed state, is_environment_reason and resumable_stop would fail.

demonstrations.method: Companion test via `Athena::go` with the same fixtures and the same check_seam (added in step 4). The seam returns a failed CheckRun with exit_code Some(1), passed false and an ordinary note. Assert state == Rejected, reason is 'check probe failed', !is_environment_reason(reason) and !resumable_stop. A unit test in checks.rs also asserts timed_out is false for exit 3, a pass, the kill-switch note, a spawn failure and a skipped run. The existing test produce_dir_is_removed_after_checks_pass_and_kept_when_a_check_fails (a real `sh -c test` failure ending Rejected) is a regression guard.
demonstrations.observes: A genuine nonzero-exit check still produces the Rejected outcome, not an environment stop.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the classifier treated every failed check (or every exit_code None) as a timeout, this job would end Failed with an environment reason instead of Rejected, and the test would fail.

demonstrations.method: In the criterion-2 test, additionally assert that the Finished reason and a line captured by the Lines UI (starting `failed     `) contain `905s of 1800s limit` (test config from the repository athena.toml via repo(), now 1800; duration 905 from the fake seam). A disk.rs unit test checks `check_timeout_reason` text directly: contains the check name, '905s of 900s limit', 'not the work' and `athena retry <job>`. The criterion-1 config test covers the 1800 load.
demonstrations.observes: Both the closing reason and the printed `failed` line carry the measured duration against the limit; the config loads with 1800.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the duration and limit in the reason, the substring assertions on the closing reason, the UI line and the disk.rs text test fail.

demonstrations.method: Grep disk.rs for `CHECK_TIMEOUT` and its use in is_environment_reason. New unit test in disk.rs `a_check_timeout_reason_is_an_environment_reason` builds `check_timeout_reason("test", 905.0, 900, &id(1))` and asserts is_environment_reason true, resumable_stop(Closed(Failed), Some(&r)) true, resumable_stop(Closed(Rejected), Some(&r)) false, and that 'check test failed' and an admission-refused reason are not environment reasons. No seam; pure functions.
demonstrations.observes: The reason is classified as environment and only a Failed close is resumable.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new prefix in is_environment_reason, the assertion that the timeout reason is an environment reason, and resumable_stop for a Failed job with it, fail.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks in order after `cargo fmt --all` has been applied (step 8). They exercise the whole workspace including the new tests of criteria 2-5 and 7's unaffected suite; the cfg(test) seam is guarded by cfg(test) on both definition and use so non-test builds have no dead code. No seam of its own.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0: formatting is canonical, clippy reports no warning (no dead code from timed_out, check_timeout_reason, deadline_note or the seam; no unused imports), and every test, old and new, passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the classification the new timeout tests in `cargo test --locked` fail (job ends Rejected); a helper added but not wired into check_and_verify (timed_out or check_timeout_reason unused) makes `clippy -D warnings` fail with a dead-code error; unformatted new code makes `cargo fmt --all --check` exit non-zero; a broken existing test, such as a hard-coded 900 limit, fails `cargo test --locked`.

demonstrations.method: Content check: Grep CHANGELOG.md for `20261026-232434-6wfq` and `check timed out`. The [Unreleased] entry names the 1800 s limit, the timeout-as-environment-stop (`environment: check timed out`, held, `athena retry`), the printed duration against the limit, the root cause (900 s limit below the 750-940 s suite time and a killed check recorded as failed) and notes the status report is a follow-up.
demonstrations.observes: The entry exists and cites the job; the existing tests that read CHANGELOG.md (if any) still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the entry, Grep for the job id in CHANGELOG.md finds nothing (the content criterion is unmet).

open_questions: A retried job whose suite still exceeds 1800 s will time out again and be held again each time; no retry cap exists in this change. Acceptable until the status report (follow-up) shows the durations?
On retry the resume mark is at stage Checks, so all checks re-run from scratch; the code read does not show whether retry also re-runs the baseline. That is existing behavior and is not changed here.
The replay stage in run/mod.rs also uses check_timeout_s as its timeout; it benefits from the higher limit and is left as is.
